svg.title: On site and in simulation
svg.desc: Three columns. Left: what the software talks to on site. Middle: the production software, which is the same in both cases. Right: the stand-in that replaces each real thing in a simulation.

g.text: <N> is an id: AGV-1 runs as /agv/a1/sim, bay B21's nodes are /bay/b21/... . On site the AGVs are reached through agvhito's proxy_node, which the simulation does not start.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: A simulation keeps every piece of production software and replaces only what is outside it: people, hardware and the clock. Each row shows one real thing, the software that talks to it, and the

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: stand-in that takes its place. The scheduler never talks to hardware, so it cannot tell the difference.
